<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **86** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-defs/17.api__CreateViewRequest.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-defs/18.api__CrudEndpointPattern.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d26556ab74c39abd96cd3056f0605693de27cd3` — the merge of head `1ee5841c092cdc7d2c446ab1e7cf933b940e3e25` into base `97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d26556ab74c39abd96cd3056f0605693de27cd3 && git checkout 3d26556ab74c39abd96cd3056f0605693de27cd3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1 1ee5841c092cdc7d2c446ab1e7cf933b940e3e25 && git checkout -B drift-repro 97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1 && git merge --no-ff 1ee5841c092cdc7d2c446ab1e7cf933b940e3e25

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 97005aed04a069abc2d2fa82fd6c1594aebd7cd1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1ee5841c092cdc7d2c446ab1e7cf933b940e3e25`
Local-runs: probe — one scratch script over the repo's git objects, tokenising the merge-base and head blobs of the 86 changed `.ts` files with a TypeScript scanner (comments and whitespace dropped) to settle comment-only; nothing built, tested or re-run.

Read: card #20234, body and all 41 comments (the C+D path decision `5856637615`, the pointer `5858331362`, stage 8's landing `5896689039`, stage 9's ACCEPT `5899135835` and landing `5899597998`, the stage-10 claim `5901544565`, the dev report `5902687602`); PR #20750, its body, its one comment, its 88-file list and the net diff against `main` at the merge base `01e78dceef`; the 21 anchor commits by `git show` and `git log`; the check-runs on the head, read once.

### ① Derived judgments

The claim says no accept-set or public-surface move. Each judgment below is from the diff and the git objects, not the dev's prose.

- **Comment-only, proven.** The token probe finds the non-trivia token streams of all 86 changed `.ts` files (85 entries plus `registry.ts`) identical between merge base and head, and its control (one string literal mutated in memory) is detected. So no entry id, verdict, order, `conversionIds`, string, template, regex or code token moved. Independently, every one of the 133 changed entry lines (132 `.ts` pairs plus one README line) and every one of the 128 changed registry lines begins with a `//` marker. RIGHT.
- **`registry.ts` moves only in its generated regions.** The os-generated markers stand at the same twelve lines at base and head. Mapping each of the 256 changed registry lines to a region: semantic:18 two, retired-key:17 four, retired-key:18 one hundred and fifty, retired-def:17 two, retired-def:18 ninety-eight, outside any region zero. The 128 registry (old, new) pairs equal the entry `.ts` pairs re-indented by four spaces, with zero registry pairs lacking an entry source; the five entry pairs not carried are the README line and the four semantic anchor-block header lines the generator does not copy. No hand-written part is edited. RIGHT.
- **Scope.** 88 files: one new changeset plus 87 under `packages/spec/src/migrations/` (the entries README, 85 entries, `registry.ts`). None of the six `entries/semantic/18.*-unit-in-key.ts` files that PR #20706 edits is touched. `spec-changes.json` and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` do not move. Nothing under `conversions/`. RIGHT.
- **The anchors are true.** Each of the 21 dead numbers answers 404 today (controls: #20234 200, #8710 404), and each now names a commit whose own content names that number (`git show` hit counts from 2 to 85 per pair). Checked against the commits themselves:
  - The four NEW anchors. `db16b9424` is the squash of PR #14526 (its subject), and its sixth sub-commit registers the ADR-0087 entry with "Registration requested on #14996; the landing PR is #14526", so the #14526 and #14996 lines are both true. `e944fdb24` is PR #15445's squash, whose body says `oauth.applications.delete` "is deliberately NOT bound" because "binding it needs a behaviour change", which is the rewritten wording. `f60ab90ae`'s changeset carries "#14365 proposes `z.partialRecord` for this record", so "the open `z.partialRecord` question (commit f60ab90ae)" points at the one in-repo record of that question rather than claiming the commit decided it, the right rung when the card is gone. `4bfe1a539` is PR #8666, and its second sub-commit reads "register the #8495 refusal as an ADR-0087 semantic entry under protocol 18", so "the precedent of commit 4bfe1a539, PR #8666" is the precedent it was.
  - The anchors whose subject does not name the number. `9e0ba21a1` (#13135) added all thirteen entry files that carried the `#13135` header and retired the paper metadata-customization module whole, so "re-chartered, that commit executes the widened surface" is true. `b3a63d32c` (#14691) added all eleven `RestServerConfig` entries and its body names the #14369 census. `dce5cd4f0` (#11332) added the three manifest-container entries. `0c2334f6c` (#11846) added the three preview-mode entries and its changeset carries the ruling wording. `bc56e1881` (#10726) added `contributes.routes`, which `be21955ba` names as the open fork. `a3d5724c8` (#14369) is the ledger commit whose rows read "seeded 2026-09-02 (#14369)" and whose body counts "15 are dead", so "the liveness census commit a3d5724c8 recorded" is true.
  - The reused anchors. `2c86fe3ea` (#8715; "Route 3 retirement kit" in its body), `be21955ba` (#10724 by subject; the #10627 reading and the 2026-08-24 cloud reading `@5b5925a` both recorded in its body, so "that commit's census" and "the cloud census" are true), `35ad101bc` (#10485), `13c48c2a5` (#14676), `90bbf2510` (#6361; "ruled jointly with #6363" in its body), `17d095413` (#6363, the `unreadCount` fix, so "the `unreadCount` fix, commit 17d095413" is true), `f549a0d4a` (#6239, the ViewProtocol sweep), `d491625c1` (#9041, the url-branch refinement whose composed twin `00777a0a6a` is #9147's).
  - The two `17.*` entry files were split out of `registry.ts` by `f293d454b7`, not by their anchors; the anchors are the commits that first wrote the decision into the registry (`git log -S` puts `90bbf2510` and `f549a0d4a` first), which is the right reading of "the commit that decided it". RIGHT.
- **The words.** Where a line lost its number, the sentence is true to the commit it names: the README's "Measured while landing commit db16b9424" describes the census-test incident that squash's own sub-commits fix ("slice census methods on masked source"); "(the #8586 / commit 2c86fe3ea precedent)", "(the commit 0c2334f6c / #12428 grading)" and "(the precedent of commit 4bfe1a539, PR #8666)" keep the live number beside the commit and the PR as a link only, ruling C's form. RIGHT.
- **Nothing lit removed, nothing added.** The numbers on removed lines that do not reappear on added lines are exactly the 21 dead numbers. The numbers on added lines are #8586, #8666, #9147, #12057, #12428 and #15445, all answering 200, all already on the same lines at base. No number appears only at head. RIGHT.
- **Census.** Read from the dev's report and the diff, not re-run: `packages/spec/src` 235 to 4, `migrations/` 233 to 2, entries 117 to 0, registry generated regions 114 to 0, hand-written 2 to 2; 254 base-only sites, of which 231 are this diff's (117 plus 114 copies) and 23 are `main`'s own `plugin-audit` re-anchor (`4dfff176b9`, PR #20737, on `main`'s log); 0 head-only. The arithmetic matches the diff: 133 changed lines, 131 dead-number sites, the two lines without a number being the `patterns` follow-on and the oauth continuation. RIGHT.
- **No accept-set or public-surface move.** Follows from comment-only; `Spec property liveness` and the three concluded `Type Check` legs are green on this head. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` is right, and its stated reason holds.** The diff is comment text, but the comments ship: at this head `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` lists `src/migrations/index.ts` as a bundle entry and `package.json` exports `./migrations` to `dist/migrations/index.mjs` and `index.js` (the shared checkout's HEAD, two days older, has neither, which is why the dev's dist measurement is not reproducible there). That the bundler keeps `//` comments is verified on the published `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tarball: its `dist/index.mjs` carries 9,901 comment lines, the old "PR #8666 precedent" phrase 23 times, and the `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` table with its entry comments. So the compiled `@objectstack/spec/migrations` entry carries these comments and the changeset's rationale sentence is true. No export, schema, prescription or projected text moves, so nothing above `patch` applies. `Check Changeset` is green.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right**, in the PR body and as a standalone line in the changeset: no accept or reject moves, by the comment-only proof.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Scope judgment (the gate's census reads 117, under the ~120 slice threshold; the raw walk 131).** The claim names the gate's own census as the instrument, so 117 governs; taking all of `entries/**` without a slice is right. Answered.
- **The dev's open question: 13 dead sites left in `registry.ts`'s hand-written parts** (two comments, :5940 #8495 and :22819 #6239; eleven author-shown rationale strings, including step 17's :344 #6345 behind guide :68). Confirmed the claim forbade touching them: `registry.ts` appears only under "Regenerated only" with "Nothing is hand-edited", and both residual comment sites sit outside the os-generated regions (:5940 in step 18's doc comment above the semantic:18 opener; :22819 between the retired-key:18 closer and the retired-def:17 opener). The claim's own guide-:68 expectation conflicts with that ⛔; the dev honoured the ⛔ and reported, the right side of "stop on breach". Leaving them is not a gap in this stage: they are a different edit kind (form D wording, reviewed sentence by sentence as stage 9 was), and this PR's comment-only proof stays exact because of it. Option A, a next stage of #20234 for `registry.ts`'s hand-written parts plus `gen:upgrade-guide`, fits. Answered.
- **Two lines change without a number** (the `patterns` follow-on, the oauth continuation): sentence continuity only. Answered.
- **Merges.** `main` has since moved to `9c8f113c64`, three commits past the second merge base `01e78dceef`, none touching `packages/spec`; the PR's recorded base `97005aed04` is one behind. No spec artifact can be jointly stale, and the queue rebuilds regardless. Answered.
- **NOT MEASURED locally** (`build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`, `def-key-collisions`, the two `publish-smoke-*` files): left to `Test Core`, which had not concluded at the read below. Named, not presumed.
- **Attribution.** The three authored commits carry the model-free trailer pair; the two merge commits carry none. Fine.
- **Labels untouched, scratch-directory reuse, the background gate batch, the kept worktree, hypothesis 6 falsified by construction:** no action owed.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the census reads `re-charter #N` as an ordinal.** `NON_CITATION_HEADS` carries `re-charter` as a deliberate row ("re-charter round ordinals"), so a five-digit tracker number after it is skipped by the heuristic's design, not by accident; still, thirteen dead sites at base were invisible to the gate's count, which is a wrong census result anyone running `--census` reaches. My read: card-worthy (a bounded fix, for instance an ordinal is at most two digits), filed unassigned; not a blocker here, since this diff rewrites the sites anyway. ESCALATED to the seat as a filing decision.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `.md` under `packages/**/src` is outside the census.** The gate's surface is the declared glob `packages/**/src/**/*.ts`, and its header says a deferred surface is a decision, not an omission. Acceptance note. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `packages/spec/liveness/*.json` carries #14691 and #14365 in REMOVED notes.** The liveness-JSON class is already on this card (pointer `5858331362`, #13003 in `permission.json`) and outside every citation instrument's declared surface, so it is a staging note on #20234, not a new card and not a wrong result of any instrument. Answered.

**Check-runs on the head, read once** in the first CI wave (the newest concluded run at the read was `Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)`), not re-read and not polled. 32 runs: 17 success, 3 skipped, 12 in progress, 0 failed.
